published_results.notes: The documented harness scripts (test-rpc-cross-replica.mjs, hammer.mjs, network-loss.mjs, test-multiprocess.mjs) are NOT present in packages/happy-server/deploy/integration-tests/ (which holds stress-*.mjs, test-rpc-dead-daemon.mjs, run-all.sh), so the gauntlet output cannot be reproduced from the clone.

summary: Happy publishes no results about agent quality; its quantitative evidence is client/server engineering performance. The iOS perf gym is the strongest piece: a runnable harness (gym.py + UI tests) with committed before/after JSON baselines that match the doc tables (e.g. scroll-while-streaming hitch 683 -> 0), though fresh runs need Xcode, a simulator and a pinned agent binary; Android cold-start and iOS sync/apply numbers have in-repo harnesses but results only in markdown, and the server chaos results reference scripts missing from the clone.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
